context.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at 3,000 TPS while supporting analyst case management. It operates in AWS eu-west-1 within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget, meeting PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year audit retention.

## Key Elements
* Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (System of Interest)
* Payment Gateway / Core Processing System (External Actor)
* Fraud Analysts and ML Engineers (External Actors)
* Card Schemes / Tokenization Service (External System)
* AWS ECS Fargate, Application Load Balancer, and Global Accelerator (Containers)
* AWS S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS (Containers/Storage)
* AWS CloudWatch and AWS X-Ray (Containers/Observability)

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway to Screening System via synchronous gRPC over TLS with mTLS and AWS IAM Signature v4 (R-01, R-04)
* Fraud Analysts to Screening System via HTTPS with RBAC, IAM/OIDC, and mandatory MFA (R-02)
* Screening System to Tokenization Service via secure API for PAN tokenization (R-05)
* Screening System to S3 Audit Archive via AWS KMS-encrypted writes with S3 Object Lock (R-06)

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS Fargate with provisioned capacity: Guarantees sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS without serverless cold starts
* gRPC over TLS: Minimizes serialization overhead to meet high-throughput performance requirements
* AWS S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode) with AWS KMS: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year audit retention
* AWS CloudWatch and AWS X-Ray: Provides low-overhead telemetry manageable by a 3-engineer team
* Local cached fallback engine: Enforces high availability without bypassing fraud checks (R-07)

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services on ECS Fargate to balance sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS with a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It strictly enforces PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditing for a 3-person engineering team.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud to approve, decline, or route them for analyst review. It maintains strict PCI-DSS compliance while processing 3,000 transactions per second under a 50ms P99 latency SLA.]

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing System
- AWS API Gateway / ALB (Ingress)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Go microservice on ECS Fargate)
- ONNX Model Sidecar container
- Case Management App (Node.js/React monolith on ECS Fargate)
- Amazon DynamoDB (Feature store and audit logs)
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL (Case management data)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock (7-year tamper-evident audit storage)
- Amazon EventBridge (Asynchronous event bus)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway calls AWS API Gateway via gRPC over TLS
- Fraud Scoring Engine queries ONNX Model Sidecar via localhost gRPC
- Fraud Scoring Engine reads/writes features to DynamoDB via AWS SDK
- Fraud Scoring Engine emits decision events to Amazon EventBridge
- Fraud Analysts access Case Management App via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Serverless container orchestration to minimize operational overhead for a 3-engineer team
- Go: Compiled language for the scoring engine to meet the <50ms P99 latency requirement
- ONNX Runtime: Lightweight model serving sidecar for seamless fraud model updates
- Amazon DynamoDB: Low-latency NoSQL data store for real-time feature lookups
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Immutable storage satisfying 7-year audit retention within budget

## Rationale
[This serverless container architecture meets strict latency, compliance, and budget constraints by leveraging AWS managed services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team. High availability, robust security controls, and immutable audit logging ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and fault tolerance.]

AWS API Gateway / ALB (Ingress).analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and provides case management for human analysts. It operates within strict latency, budget, and compliance constraints on AWS.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing System
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) & AWS WAFv2 (Ingress)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Go microservice on Amazon ECS Fargate with ONNX Runtime sidecar)
- Case Management App (Node.js/React monolith on Amazon ECS Fargate)
- Data Stores: Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon RDS PostgreSQL, Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- Event Bus: Amazon EventBridge
- Fraud Analysts and ML Engineers

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> AWS Application Load Balancer: Sends authorization requests [gRPC over mTLS 1.3]
- AWS Application Load Balancer -> AWS WAFv2: Inspects request headers and payloads [Internal AWS]
- AWS Application Load Balancer -> Fraud Scoring Engine: Forwards validated requests via target groups [gRPC over HTTP/2]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Amazon DynamoDB: Reads feature stores and writes audit logs [AWS PrivateLink]
- Case Management App -> Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Manages analyst review cases [SQL over TLS]

## Technology Stack
- Ingress/Security: AWS Application Load Balancer, AWS WAFv2, AWS Certificate Manager for TLS 1.3/mTLS (cost-effective, predictable pricing for 3,000 req/s)
- Compute: Amazon ECS Fargate (container orchestration tailored for a 3-engineer team)
- Scoring Core: Go microservice with ONNX Runtime sidecar (meets <50 ms P99 latency SLA)
- Storage & Audit: Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon RDS PostgreSQL, Amazon S3 with Object Lock (ensures 7-year tamper-evident auditability and PCI-DSS compliance)
- Automation: Terraform (enables repeatable, zero-manual-drift deployments)

## Rationale
This architecture leverages AWS serverless and managed containers (ECS Fargate, ALB) to meet the 3,000 req/s and <50 ms P99 latency SLAs within a fixed €25k/month budget. Strict mTLS, WAF log scrubbing, and S3 Object Lock satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident audit requirements.

Fraud Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Fraud Scoring Engine evaluates real-time payment authorization requests for fraud using a high-performance Go microservice deployed on AWS. It delivers sub-50ms decisions at 3,000 TPS while ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditing.

## Key Elements
* API Handler (Go): Manages ingress validation, sanitization, and mTLS termination.
* Feature Assembler (Go): Fetches real-time behavioral features concurrently with built-in circuit breakers.
* Rule Engine (Go): Evaluates deterministic business rules in-memory to bypass ML inference.
* Inference Client (Go): Interfaces with the ONNX Model Sidecar via localhost gRPC.
* Audit Logger (Go): Asynchronously signs and records decision payloads via AWS KMS.
* ONNX Model Sidecar (ONNX Runtime): Executes machine learning model scoring.

## Relationships
* AWS API Gateway / ALB -> API Handler: Routes incoming payment requests [HTTPS/mTLS]
* API Handler -> Rule Engine / Feature Assembler: Passes sanitized transaction data [In-memory function calls]
* Feature Assembler -> Amazon DynamoDB: Queries behavioral features and audit logs [AWS SDK / TLS]
* Inference Client -> ONNX Model Sidecar: Executes model inference queries [localhost gRPC]
* Audit Logger -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Persists signed audit trails [AWS SDK / TLS]
* Fraud Scoring Engine -> Amazon EventBridge: Emits decision events [API / Event Bus]

## Technology Stack
* Go: Chosen for concurrency model (goroutines) and low memory footprint to hit sub-50ms latency targets.
* ONNX Runtime: Provides lightweight, high-performance machine learning model execution.
* Amazon ECS Fargate: Runs containers without server management to fit the 3-engineer operational capacity.
* Amazon DynamoDB: Delivers predictable single-digit millisecond latency for feature retrieval.
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock & AWS KMS: Ensures tamper-evident, encrypted 7-year audit storage.
* AWS Application Auto Scaling: Manages traffic spikes dynamically to maintain performance under budget constraints.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Go and containerized services on AWS Fargate to meet strict sub-50ms P99 latency and high-throughput requirements within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Security and compliance controls—including tokenization, mTLS, and AWS KMS-signed audit logs—satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit retention mandates.

ONNX Model Sidecar.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and manage reviews. It ensures high-performance scoring and tamper-evident auditability within PCI-DSS and budget constraints.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts and ML Engineers
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing System
- Card Schemes / Tokenization Service
- AWS API Gateway / ALB
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Go microservice on Amazon ECS Fargate)
- ONNX Model Sidecar (ONNX Runtime C++ API)
- Case Management App (Node.js/React monolith on ECS Fargate)
- Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon RDS PostgreSQL
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- Amazon EventBridge

## Relationships
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> ONNX Model Sidecar: Sends feature tensors for scoring [`Unix Domain Sockets (UDS) gRPC`]
- Model Hot-Loader Component -> Amazon S3: Downloads `.onnx` model and signature manifest [`HTTPS / TLS 1.3`]
- Ingress -> AWS API Gateway / ALB: Routes incoming authorization traffic [`HTTPS`]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget constraint.
- ONNX Runtime (C++ API): High-performance execution runtime avoiding garbage collection pauses to meet P99 < 50ms latency.
- Amazon DynamoDB & RDS PostgreSQL: Scalable persistence for case management and immutable audit trails.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Tamper-evident 7-year retention storage for decisions and models.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages lightweight sidecar patterns and Unix Domain Sockets to achieve sub-50ms fraud scoring latency on AWS Fargate. Strict security hardening, scoped IAM roles, and cryptographic model verification ensure full PCI-DSS compliance and robust auditability.

Case Management App.analysis:
## Overview
A real-time payment fraud screening system processes card-not-present transactions, while providing fraud analysts a secure case management interface. It ensures sub-50ms P99 decisions at 3,000 TPS under PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- **API Controller Component (Express.js)**: Handles routing, OIDC/MFA authentication, rate limiting, and RBAC.
- **Case Service Component (TypeScript)**: Manages case workflows, business logic, and Prisma ORM interactions.
- **UI SPA Component (React / Tailwind CSS)**: Renders the analyst dashboard with masked card data.
- **Audit & Compliance Component (TypeScript)**: Generates structured, immutable audit logs.
- **Tokenization Gateway Client (TypeScript)**: Communicates with external tokenization services via mTLS.
- **Amazon RDS Proxy**: Pools database connections and enforces TLS.
- **Amazon RDS PostgreSQL**: Persists relational case data.
- **Amazon CloudWatch Logs & S3 with Object Lock**: Stores tamper-evident, KMS-encrypted audit trails.
- **AWS ECS Fargate & Application Load Balancer**: Runs containers with autoscaling, managed by a three-engineer team.

## Relationships
- **Fraud Analysts** -> **API Controller Component**: Views and updates case statuses [HTTPS/TLS 1.3 with MFA]
- **API Controller Component** -> **Case Service Component**: Delegates business logic [In-memory]
- **Case Service Component** -> **Tokenization Gateway Client**: Requests masked card data [HTTPS/REST with mTLS]
- **Case Service Component** -> **Amazon RDS Proxy**: Persists case data [TCP/TLS]
- **Case Service Component** -> **Audit & Compliance Component**: Dispatches audit events [In-memory]
- **Audit & Compliance Component** -> **Amazon CloudWatch Logs**: Streams structured JSON logs [AWS Firelens/HTTPS]
- **Amazon CloudWatch Logs** -> **Amazon S3 with Object Lock**: Archives immutable logs [Subscription Filter]

## Technology Stack
- **Node.js / Express.js / TypeScript**: Powers backend components for robust, typed service logic within a small team's skill set.
- **React / Tailwind CSS**: Renders a responsive analyst UI served via containerized monolith.
- **Prisma ORM & Amazon RDS PostgreSQL**: Provides type-safe database access and reliable relational storage.
- **Amazon RDS Proxy**: Prevents connection exhaustion during Fargate scaling events.
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Minimizes operational overhead within the €25k/month budget.
- **Amazon S3 with Object Lock & CloudWatch Logs**: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year audit compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict PCI-DSS security, 7-year auditability, and sub-50ms performance requirements using fully managed AWS services. By leveraging serverless containers (ECS Fargate) and managed proxies (RDS Proxy), it maintains high availability within a fixed budget for a three-engineer team.

Amazon DynamoDB.analysis:
## Overview
Amazon DynamoDB serves as a low-latency feature store and append-only audit log store for real-time payment fraud screening. It enables sub-50ms fraud decisions while strictly maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year audit trail.

## Key Elements
* **`FeatureStore` Table:** DynamoDB table using Provisioned Capacity with Auto-Scaling, optimized for low-latency point reads.
* **`AuditLogs` Table:** DynamoDB table capturing append-only decision logs synced via DynamoDB Streams.
* **AWS VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink):** Secures data-in-transit between ECS containers and DynamoDB.
* **AWS KMS CMK:** Encrypts data at rest using Customer Managed Keys with automated rotation.
* **Terraform Modules:** Infrastructure-as-Code engine defining tables, auto-scaling, and endpoints.
* **Amazon CloudWatch:** Monitors `ReadThrottleEvents`, `SystemErrors`, and Contributor Insights.

## Relationships
* **Fraud Scoring Engine -> `FeatureStore`:** Executes single-digit millisecond `GetItem` and `BatchGetItem` calls via AWS SDK over HTTPS / VPC Endpoint.
* **`AuditLogs` -> Amazon S3 (Object Lock):** Streams tamper-evident decision logs asynchronously via DynamoDB Streams using AWS SDK.
* **Case Management App -> `FeatureStore` & `AuditLogs`:** Executes restricted `Query` operations via AWS SDK governed by ABAC IAM policies.
* **Amazon CloudWatch -> Amazon SNS / PagerDuty:** Triggers automated failover alerts on throttling or system errors.

## Technology Stack
* **Amazon DynamoDB:** Chosen for predictable single-digit millisecond latency at 3,000 TPS under fixed cost constraints.
* **Provisioned Capacity with Auto-Scaling:** Selected over On-Demand to prevent budget spikes while handling 3,000 TPS.
* **AWS Encryption SDK:** Implemented for client-side attribute-level encryption to satisfy PCI-DSS scope reduction.
* **AWS VPC Endpoints:** Mandated to ensure payment traffic bypasses the public internet.
* **Terraform:** Used for repeatable, version-controlled infrastructure deployment.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees P99 latency below 50ms at 3,000 TPS through composite primary keys (`MerchantID#CustomerID`) and provisioned capacity. It respects the 25,000 EUR monthly budget and PCI-DSS Level 1 constraints via VPC isolation, AWS KMS encryption, and automated compliance auditing.

Amazon RDS PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
The Amazon RDS PostgreSQL component serves as the secure, durable relational data store for case management data in the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system. It provides structured storage for analyst reviews and investigation notes while strictly complying with PCI-DSS Level 1 mandates.

## Key Elements
- **Case Management Schema**: Relational tables storing analyst reviews, investigation notes, and case statuses.
- **pgBouncer Connection Pooler**: Manages database connections from ephemeral ECS Fargate tasks.
- **pgaudit Extension**: Logs all DDL, DCL, and privileged DML statements for compliance.

## Relationships
- **Case Management App -> Case Management Schema**: Reads and writes case data via TCP/SSL (Port 5432) using `pgBouncer`.
- **Amazon RDS PostgreSQL -> AWS Backup**: Performs automated snapshots and WAL archiving via AWS API for 7-year retention.

## Technology Stack
- **PostgreSQL 15 Engine**: Relational database core selected for robust ACID guarantees and schema management.
- **AWS Secrets Manager & IAM Database Authentication**: Manages credentials securely without hardcoded passwords.
- **AWS KMS (AES-256):** Encrypts data at rest using customer-managed keys.

## Rationale
This architecture offloads high-throughput logging to S3, protecting relational integrity for low-frequency case management. It aligns with team capacity and budget by leveraging fully managed AWS services for high availability and compliance.

Amazon S3 with Object Lock.analysis:
## Overview
This architecture implements a tamper-evident, 7-year audit storage solution using AWS S3 for a real-time payment fraud screening system. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining cost-efficiency for a three-person engineering team.

## Key Elements
* **Amazon S3 Bucket**: Core storage configured in S3 Compliance Mode with Object Lock for unalterable 7-year retention.
* **AWS KMS**: Manages customer-managed encryption keys (CMK) for server-side encryption.
* **Amazon S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint**: Enforces private, zero-trust network routing from the Fraud Scoring Engine.
* **S3 Lifecycle Management Engine**: Automatically transitions aged audit records to S3 Glacier Flexible Archive.
* **Cross-Region Replication (CRR)**: Replicates encrypted audit payloads to a secondary region (`eu-central-1`) for disaster recovery.

## Relationships
* **Fraud Scoring Engine** *writes* audit payloads to **Amazon S3 Bucket** via **Amazon S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint** using HTTPS (TLS 1.3).
* **Amazon S3 Bucket** *uses* **AWS KMS** for encryption-at-rest.
* **S3 Lifecycle Management Engine** *transitions* aged audit objects to **S3 Glacier Flexible Archive**.
* **Amazon S3 Bucket** *replicates* encrypted data to the secondary region storage via **Cross-Region Replication (CRR)**.

## Technology Stack
* **Amazon S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode)**: Enforces strict write-once-read-many (WORM) constraints for mandatory 7-year audit retention.
* **AWS KMS**: Provides customer-managed encryption keys to meet strict cardholder data protection mandates.
* **Amazon S3 Lifecycle Policies**: Optimizes storage costs by shifting high-volume 3,000 TPS logs to archival storage.
* **Amazon S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint**: Secures network transit without incurring NAT gateway costs or exposing data to the public internet.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and unalterable auditability (R-06) through S3 Object Lock and KMS encryption. Automated lifecycle management and VPC endpoints balance strict security and disaster recovery requirements within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Amazon EventBridge.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system processes card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor. It screens transactions for fraud before approval and provides case management for analysts reviewing suspicious payments.

## Key Elements
- Rule Evaluation Bus (Amazon EventBridge custom event bus)
- Event Archive & Replay Component (EventBridge Archive)
- Dead Letter Queue Handler (SQS + EventBridge DLQ)
- Event Schema Registry (EventBridge Schema Registry)

## Relationships
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Rule Evaluation Bus: Publishes payment decision events via `PutEvents` [HTTPS / JSON]
- Rule Evaluation Bus -> Case Management App: Routes review decisions [HTTPS / EventBridge Target]
- Rule Evaluation Bus -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Forwards audit events [Firehose / HTTPS]
- Rule Evaluation Bus -> Event Schema Registry: Enforces payload validation [EventBridge API / JSON Schema]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon EventBridge: Provides managed event routing within a €25k/month budget
- AWS IAM & KMS: Enforces least-privilege access and data encryption at rest for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance
- AWS CloudWatch & X-Ray: Delivers observability, distributed tracing, and automated alerting

## Rationale
This architecture meets PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 50 ms P99 latency constraint while remaining manageable for a three-engineer team. It guarantees tamper-evident 7-year auditability and high availability via native AWS serverless components.
